# Cycle 0001 Insight

## Cohort outcome

The cohort tried three small, single-axis changes to the S3-FIFO baseline: tightening the small-queue promotion bar, re-routing ghost-hit re-admissions, and shrinking the small admission queue. Only one variant hurt hit-rate, and no variant measurably improved any dimension, so both Winners (v002, v003) are neutral rather than improvements.

## Patterns

- Nothing moved hit-rate upward. Both Winners reported no change from the parent on the single trace measured, so the Winner label reflects "did not regress" rather than a demonstrated gain.
- The two-hit promotion bar appears to be doing useful filtering. Relaxing it to one hit displaced main-queue residents and cost hits.
- The ghost re-admission axis and the small-queue sizing axis both looked inert on this workload. Changes there produced no measurable effect.
- Every variant reported only hit-rate. Metadata-size and per-op-time were not assessed in any variant, so cost-side tradeoffs are unknown.
- All evidence comes from one trace (lirs workload-a) at one capacity (2048), so none of these results generalize yet.

## Open questions

- Do the neutral results for ghost routing and small-queue sizing hold at other capacities or on other workloads, or is this trace simply insensitive to them?
- Would a larger change to the small-queue sizing, rather than a one-constant tweak, move hit-rate at all?
- What do the metadata and per-op-time costs look like for these variants? Without them, a neutral hit-rate cannot be ranked against the baseline.

## Continuation

Drop the promotion-bar relaxation; it is a measured loss on this trace. Do not spend the next cycle on small tweaks to ghost routing or small-queue ratio at this single capacity, since they showed no signal. Next cycle should test changes that report metadata-size and per-op-time alongside hit-rate, and should be checked on at least one additional trace or capacity before any variant is treated as a real gain.

# Cycle 0002 Insight

## Cohort outcome

The cohort tried a cost-side refactor of ghost-membership lookup (v001), a single-constant change to the main-queue frequency cap (v002), and a freq-layout change (v003) that did not land in the overlay. Both Winners (v001, v002) are hit-rate neutral against the parent; neither shows a demonstrated gain, and v003 showed an unexplained hit-rate drop.

## Patterns

- Hit-rate stayed flat for both Winners. v001 is a pure cost refactor that preserved eviction order, and v002 raising the main-queue frequency cap showed no effect on this trace.
- Neither Winner reported metadata-size or per-op-time, so the cost claims behind v001 are unverified. This is the same gap the prior cycle flagged; it persisted into this cohort.
- v002's null result suggests few main-queue residents on this trace build up enough hits to reach the old cap, so the frequency axis looks inert here, consistent with the prior cycle's sizing and routing findings.
- v003 did not implement its hypothesis (the layout change is absent from the overlay). Its hit-rate drop cannot be attributed to the layout idea and may reflect an overlay or build mismatch rather than the change itself.
- Evidence is still one trace (lirs workload-a) at one capacity (2048).

## Open questions

- Does the v001 ghost-lookup refactor reduce per-op-time, and at what metadata cost? It cannot be ranked on cost until both are reported.
- Is the v003 drop real, or an artifact of the mismatched overlay? Does the hit-rate drop reproduce on a clean build?
- Does the frequency cap matter at other capacities or workloads, where main-queue residents may accumulate more hits?

## Continuation

Keep the ghost-lookup refactor (v001) only as a cost candidate, and require a rerun reporting per-op-time and metadata-size before treating it as a win. Drop the frequency-cap tweak (v002) on this trace; it has now shown no signal in two cycles. Before the next cycle, verify the v003 overlay and rebuild its layout variant; do not test any layout change until the build is confirmed clean.

# Cycle 0003 Insight

## Cohort outcome

The cohort tried a resident-key lookup structure to skip queue scans on misses (v001), a higher small-queue promotion bar (v002), and a doubled ghost queue (v003). Both Winners (v001, v002) are hit-rate neutral against the parent, so neither is a demonstrated gain; v003 is the only variant that lost hit-rate.

## Patterns

- Hit-rate stayed flat for both Winners. v001 is intended as a cost-side change that should leave eviction order alone, and v002's promotion-bar change showed no effect on this trace.
- The promotion bar has now been probed in both directions across cycles: relaxing it to one hit lost hits in Cycle 0001, and raising it to three hits was neutral here. The axis looks saturated on this trace, not a source of gains.
- Widening the ghost window (v003) lost hit-rate. The variant's account is that extra ghost hits bypass the small queue and land directly in main, displacing resident entries. Ghost coverage alone does not appear to be the lever.
- Neither Winner reported metadata-size or per-op-time, so v001's cost claim is still unverified. This gap has now persisted across three cycles.
- v002 could not confirm from its overlay that the `freq > 2` edit landed, so its neutral result may not reflect the intended change. This echoes Cycle 0002's overlay problem.
- Evidence is still one trace (lirs workload-a) at one capacity (2048).

## Open questions

- Does the v001 resident-key structure reduce per-op-time, and at what metadata cost? It cannot be ranked until both are reported.
- Did the v002 edit actually land in the built code? Until that is confirmed, its flat result says nothing about the promotion bar.
- Does the ghost-window loss hold if ghost hits are admitted differently (for example, through the small queue rather than main)?

## Continuation

Keep v001's resident-key idea only as a cost candidate, and require a rerun that reports per-op-time and metadata-size before calling it a win. Drop the doubled ghost queue (v003) as a standalone change; any future ghost-size work must also change how ghost hits are admitted. Drop further promotion-bar tweaks on this trace. Before the next cycle, confirm that each overlay edit is present in the build so results can be attributed to the intended change.

# Cycle 0004 Insight

## Cohort outcome

The cohort tried a resident-key probe with early return on hits (v001), routing ghost-hit re-admissions through the small queue (v002), and a packed single-byte bitfield for queue membership and frequency (v003). Both Winners (v001, v003) are hit-rate neutral against the parent, so neither is a demonstrated gain; v002 is the only variant that lost hit-rate.

## Patterns

- Both Winners were behavior-preserving on paper and stayed flat on hit-rate, which is consistent with unchanged eviction order. Neither reported metadata-size or per-op-time, so their cost claims remain unverified. This gap has now persisted across four cycles.
- Ghost handling has now been probed in two ways. Widening the ghost window lost hits in Cycle 0003, and routing ghost hits through the small queue lost hits here. Neither direction of the ghost-admission lever has shown a gain on this trace.
- The promotion bar appears to be the likely mechanism in v002: re-admitted keys that were recently evicted and still hot must now pass the bar before counting as main-queue residents. This connects to the promotion-bar findings of earlier cycles.
- Neither Winner's source diff was confirmed in its overlay, so the flat results may not reflect the intended edits. This is the same overlay-verification gap raised in Cycles 0002 and 0003.
- Evidence is still one trace (lirs workload-a) at one capacity (2048).

## Open questions

- Do the v001 probe and v003 bitfield reduce per-op-time or metadata-size? Neither can be ranked until both are reported on a rerun.
- Did the v001 and v003 edits actually land in the built code? Until they are confirmed, their flat results cannot be attributed to the intended changes.
- Is the v002 loss specific to the two-hit promotion bar, or would ghost re-admissions do better under a different bar?

## Continuation

Keep the v001 probe and v003 bitfield only as cost candidates, and require a rerun that reports per-op-time and metadata-size, plus confirmation that the overlay edits are present, before treating either as a win. Drop ghost-admission routing through the small queue (v002) as a standalone change, since it has now lost hits in one direction after the window-widening loss in the other. Do not spend the next cycle on further ghost-window or promotion-bar tweaks on this trace.

# Cycle 0005 Insight

## Cohort outcome

The cohort tried removing a second resident-key probe on the miss path (v001), halving the main-queue frequency decay step (v002), and making the small-queue size adaptive to ghost hits (v003). Both Winners (v001, v002) are hit-rate neutral against the parent, so neither is a demonstrated gain; v003 is the only variant that lost hit-rate.

## Patterns

- Both Winners held hit-rate flat, which fits the intent of leaving eviction order alone. Neither reported metadata-size or per-op-time, so the cost claim behind v001 remains unmeasured.
- The frequency axis has now been probed again with a decay change, and it is flat, matching the earlier frequency-cap result. It looks inert on this trace.
- Making the small-queue size adaptive (v003) did not beat the fixed split. The ghost-hit signal appears too noisy to steer the target, so the sizing lever is not yet a source of gains.
- Across the recent cycles, the promotion-bar, ghost-admission, frequency, and sizing levers have all come back flat or negative on this trace.
- The overlay source could not be inspected for any variant this cycle, so none of the flat or negative results can yet be tied to the intended edits. This is the same verification gap raised in prior cycles.
- Evidence is still one trace (lirs workload-a) at one capacity (2048).

## Open questions

- Does removing the miss-path probe (v001) reduce per-op-time, and at what metadata cost? It cannot be ranked until both are reported.
- Did the v001 and v002 edits land in the built code? Until they are confirmed, their flat results say little about the intended changes.
- Would adaptive sizing behave differently with damping or a wider step, or is the ghost signal too noisy for any sizing rule on this trace?

## Continuation

Keep the v001 probe removal only as a cost candidate, and require a rerun that reports per-op-time and metadata-size, plus confirmation that the overlay edit is present, before calling it a win. Drop the frequency decay tweak (v002) as a standalone change, since the frequency axis has shown no signal across cycles. Drop the ±1 adaptive small-queue sizing (v003) as implemented. Do not spend the next cycle on further frequency or sizing tweaks on this trace; prioritize build and overlay verification plus cost reporting.

# Cycle 0006 Insight

## Cohort outcome

The cohort tried folding resident-key membership into the queue-state bit (v001), giving frequency-positive main-queue victims a tail second pass instead of a head reinsert (v002), and returning early on resident hits before the ghost lookup (v003). Both Winners (v001, v003) are cost-side changes that are hit-rate neutral against the parent, so neither is a demonstrated gain; v002 is the only variant that lost hit-rate.

## Patterns

- The two Winners both target per-op-time or metadata-size while leaving eviction order alone. Both held hit-rate flat, which fits that intent, but neither reported the cost dimensions, so their claims remain unmeasured. This gap has now persisted across several cycles.
- Longer retention of warm main-queue residents (v002) lost hit-rate on this trace. This is a new lever, distinct from the promotion-bar and ghost-admission axes, and it suggests the existing head reinsert is not leaving value on the table here.
- The v001 overlay was not inspected this cycle, and the v002 and v003 insights do not confirm their edits either. The same overlay-verification gap raised in prior cycles still applies.
- Evidence is still one trace (lirs workload-a) at one capacity (2048).

## Open questions

- Do the v001 bit-folding and v003 early return reduce per-op-time or metadata-size? Neither can be ranked until a rerun reports both.
- Did the v001, v002, and v003 edits actually land in the built code? Until they are confirmed, the flat and negative results cannot be tied to the intended changes.
- The v003 insight cites v001 as its control. Confirm that the v003 comparison baseline is the intended parent, so that its neutral result is attributed correctly.

## Continuation

Keep the v001 bit-folding and the v003 early return only as cost candidates, and require a rerun that reports per-op-time and metadata-size, plus confirmation that each overlay edit is present, before calling either a win. Drop the tail-reinsert retention change (v002) as a standalone change, since it lost hits on this trace. Do not spend the next cycle on further main-queue retention or reinsert-position tweaks; prioritize build and overlay verification and cost reporting.

# Cycle 0007 Insight

## Cohort outcome

The cohort tried replacing queue scans with a resident-key index (v001), removing the ghost-membership mirror set in favor of a linear ghost scan (v002, stacked on v001), and carrying a frequency of 1 into main on ghost re-admission (v003). Both Winners (v001, v002) are hit-rate neutral against the parent and are cost-side changes, so neither is a demonstrated gain; v003 is the only variant that lost hit-rate.

## Patterns

- The two Winners are structurally one line of work: v002 is explicitly equivalence-preserving on top of v001. Their hit-rate results therefore do not count as independent confirmations.
- Both Winners were built to leave eviction order alone and held hit-rate flat, which fits that intent. Neither reported metadata-size or per-op-time, so the O(1) and metadata claims are still unmeasured.
- v002 trades a hash mirror for a linear ghost scan. Its own insight flags a possible per-op-time cost on the miss path, so the cost direction it claims may not hold.
- Ghost re-admission has now been pushed in a third way. Widening the ghost window (Cycle 0003), routing ghost hits through the small queue (Cycle 0004), and giving re-admissions an extra main-queue pass (v003) all lost or failed to help. Ghost-admission levers look unproductive on this trace.
- The v001 and v002 insights do not confirm that their intended edits are present in the built code. The overlay-verification gap from prior cycles still applies.
- Evidence is still one trace (lirs workload-a) at one capacity (2048).

## Open questions

- Does the resident-key index (v001) reduce per-op-time, and at what metadata cost? Only a rerun reporting both can settle it.
- Does removing the ghost mirror (v002) help metadata-size enough to offset a linear miss-path scan? Its cost direction is unknown until per-op-time is measured.
- Did the v001 and v002 edits land in the built code? Their flat hit-rate results cannot be tied to the intended changes until this is confirmed.

## Continuation

Treat the resident-key index (v001) as the lead cost candidate, and require a rerun that reports per-op-time and metadata-size plus confirmation of the overlay edit before calling it a win. Hold the ghost-mirror removal (v002) until v001 is measured, since its linear scan may regress per-op-time. Drop giving ghost re-admissions a frequency of 1 (v003) as a standalone change. Do not spend the next cycle on further ghost-admission or frequency tweaks on this trace; prioritize build and overlay verification and cost reporting.

# Cycle 0008 Insight

## Cohort outcome

The cohort tried a cheaper hasher on the resident index (v001), moving small-queue second-hit entries to the front of main earlier (v002), and a counting pre-filter in front of the ghost linear scan (v003). All three Winners are hit-rate neutral against the parent, so none is a demonstrated gain; the cohort is cost-side work that has not yet been measured on cost.

## Patterns

- All three Winners held hit-rate flat, which fits their intent: each changes how work is done or when a warm key moves, not which keys are evicted. None reported per-op-time or metadata-size, so every cost claim remains unmeasured.
- Two of the three edits (v001 hasher, v003 pre-filter) are constant-factor or metadata changes on the miss path. The ghost linear scan is still untouched by v001, so any gain from it is bounded.
- The promotion-timing change (v002) showed that moving an already-warm key earlier does not alter residency. Promotion-timing levers need to change the eviction decision itself to matter.
- v003's implementation diverges from its hypothesis: counters are wider than specified, and the key is hashed on every ghost push, pop and re-admission, so the eviction path may slow even if skipped scans save time. The cost direction is genuinely uncertain.
- Overlay edits were not confirmed for any variant this cycle, the same verification gap carried since earlier cycles.
- Evidence is still one trace (lirs workload-a) at one capacity (2048).

## Open questions

- Does the hasher swap (v001) lower per-op-time on get and put, and does the ghost scan cap that gain?
- Does the ghost pre-filter (v003) save more on skipped scans than it costs in per-push hashing and wider counters? Only a rerun reporting per-op-time and metadata-size can answer this.
- Did the v001 and v003 edits land as described in the built code, and did v002's promotion edit land at all?

## Continuation

Carry the hasher swap (v001) and the ghost pre-filter (v003) forward only as cost candidates, and require a rerun that reports per-op-time and metadata-size plus confirmation of each overlay edit before calling either a win; test v003 with the counter width the hypothesis specified. Drop the earlier promotion of second-hit small entries (v002) as a standalone change, since it moved timing without changing hits. Do not spend the next cycle on further promotion-timing tweaks; prioritize build and overlay verification and cost reporting.

# Cycle 0009 Insight

## Cohort outcome

The cohort tried storing 64-bit fingerprints in the ghost queue (v001), feeding main-queue evictions at zero frequency into the ghost queue (v002), and collapsing the residency probe and insert in `put` into one entry call (v003). Only v002 is a Winner, with a small hit-rate gain on lirs workload-a at capacity 2048; v001 and v003 are hit-rate neutral and carry only unmeasured cost claims.

## Patterns

- v002 is the only variant with a measured hit-rate movement, and it is the first ghost-side change this line has produced a gain from. It changes which keys reach the ghost queue, not the ghost window, small-queue routing, or re-admission frequency, which earlier cycles tried and dropped. The gain is marginal and rests on one trace at one size.
- v001 and v003 held hit-rate identical to the parent, as their hypotheses predicted. Both are constant-factor or representation changes. Neither reports per-op-time or metadata-size, so their savings cannot be credited.
- v001 adds a second key hash on every ghost check and push while leaving the linear ghost scan and `retain` in place, so the miss-path cost may not improve at all.
- v003 calls `key.clone()` on every `put`, including hits, which may cancel the saving from the single hash for heap-allocated keys.
- v002 leaves the ghost `retain` and `any` scans unchanged, so it adds ghost entries without changing the cost of ghost lookups.
- Overlay edits were not independently confirmed for any variant this cycle. The v002 gain should be tied to its edit in the built code before it is treated as real.
- Evidence is still one trace (lirs workload-a) at one capacity (2048).

## Open questions

- Does the v002 gain hold on other traces and capacities, or is it specific to lirs workload-a at 2048?
- Does the v002 gain persist once ghost entries from main evictions are weighed against the cost of the unchanged ghost scans?
- Do the v001 fingerprint and the v003 single-hash `put` lower per-op-time or metadata-size once the extra hash and the `key.clone()` are counted?

## Continuation

Carry v002 forward as the lead hit-rate candidate: pursue main-eviction ghost feeding, and require a rerun on additional traces and at least one other capacity, plus confirmation of its overlay edit. Keep v001 and v003 only as cost candidates, and drop them as standalone changes unless a rerun reports per-op-time and metadata-size. Do not spend the next cycle on small-queue or ghost-window tweaks beyond the main-eviction feed.

# Cycle 0010 Insight

## Cohort outcome

The cohort tried a capped side ring for main-evicted zero-frequency keys (v001), replacing the linear ghost queue with a deque plus key index (v002), and feeding main-queue victims with frequency of at least 1 into the ghost queue (v003). Only v002 is a Winner, and it is hit-rate neutral, so its case rests on an unmeasured cost claim. v001 lost hit-rate and v003 was flat.

## Patterns

- The side-ring split (v001) lost the hit-rate gain that the Cycle 0009 main-eviction ghost feed produced. Keeping main-fed entries in the shared ghost window, with no tight cap, appears necessary for that gain.
- v003 fed warm victims (frequency of at least 1) into the ghost queue and was flat. Together with v001, this points to the Cycle 0009 gain coming from the cold, zero-frequency victims. Warm-key feeding adds nothing on this trace.
- v002 is a ghost-structure refactor meant to cut miss-path cost with eviction unchanged. Hit-rate held flat, as predicted, but no per-op-time or metadata-size was reported, so the speed claim is unmeasured.
- The v002 and v003 insights could not confirm their overlay edits in the built code. A flat result from v003 may be a no-op implementation, so the gap from prior cycles still applies.
- Evidence is still one trace (lirs workload-a) at one capacity (2048).

## Open questions

- Is the Cycle 0009 gain specific to cold victims, and does a cold-only feed hold on other traces and capacities?
- Does the v002 deque-and-index refactor lower per-op-time on the miss path, and at what metadata cost?
- Did the v002 and v003 edits land in the built code, and did v003's ghost push fire at all?

## Continuation

Carry the cold-victim main-eviction ghost feed from Cycle 0009 (v002 of that cycle) forward as the lead hit-rate candidate. Do not pursue a capped side ring for main-fed entries (v001) or a warm-victim feed (v003) as standalone changes. Treat the ghost refactor (v002) as a cost candidate only, and require a rerun that reports per-op-time and metadata-size plus overlay confirmation before calling it a win.
